name: Learn basic perspective drawing
blurb: One-, two- and three-point perspective are geometric rules, not art talent. Once you have them, drawing convincing rooms, streets and boxes becomes procedural.
gear: A viewfinder or a phone camera
steps: Learn the horizon line as eye level, and understand that it moves with you rather than with the scene.
Learn one-point perspective by drawing a corridor and a room interior with all depth lines meeting one vanishing point.
Learn two-point perspective by drawing a building corner with two vanishing points on the horizon.
Learn to divide space in perspective — the diagonal method for equal spacing of fence posts, windows and floor tiles.
Learn three-point perspective for looking up at or down on tall structures.
Draw a real street scene from observation and check your lines against the photo.
tips: Vanishing points placed too close together produce a violently distorted image. Push them further out, usually off the page.
Everything shares the same horizon line. That is what makes a scene cohere.
proof: You draw a convincing street scene in two-point perspective from imagination, with consistent vanishing points.
